Goal

This notebook asks whether HUC8-scale GPP and ER allometries vary systematically across broad Level I ecoregions. The intent is descriptive stratification: ecoregions are used to summarize where scaling patterns occur, not to infer that ecoregion membership causes those scaling patterns.

My take:

Build or read the HUC8 ecoregion lookup

This section uses a lightweight API route. It queries the ArcGIS REST service for Level I North American terrestrial ecoregions, assigns each HUC8 to the Level I ecoregion containing its point-on-surface, and saves only the small HUC8 lookup table. The ecoregion polygons themselves are not saved.

How do GPP and ER slopes vary across Level I ecoregions?

My take:

Where do GPP and ER scaling rules diverge?

Positive values mean GPP has the steeper annual allometric slope. Negative values mean ER has the steeper annual allometric slope.

My take:

Are ecoregion patterns seasonal?

This heatmap shows the median monthly HUC8 allometric slope within each Level I ecoregion. It is a compact way to see whether ecoregion separation is persistent or season-specific.

My take:

Do ecoregion differences persist after excluding compromised HUC8s?

This is a quick sensitivity check. “Compromised” follows the centroid-filter diagnostics from the 06 workflow. It does not mean the HUC8 is unusable; it only flags HUC8s where removed reaches may have enough leverage to matter.

My take:

How does null-model support vary across ecoregions?

This summarizes the 06a null-model coherence results by ecoregion. It is still descriptive: a high ecoregion value means that HUC8-month tests in that ecoregion often exceeded the shuffled-network null, not that ecoregion properties caused the coherence.
